name: Lew Wallace
bio: Lew (Lewis) Wallace was an American soldier, lawyer, diplomat and novelist, born in Brookville, Indiana, in 1827, who rose to the rank of general in the Civil War and was United States minister to Turkey from 1881 to 1885.
He is best known for the novel Ben-Hur (1880); he also wrote The Fair God (1873) and The Prince of India (1893).

poems.title: Song from “Ben Hur”
poems.author: Lew Wallace
poems.text:
Wake not, but hear me, love!
Adrift, adrift on slumber’s sea,
Thy spirit call to list to me.
Wake not, but hear me, love!

A gift from Sleep, the restful king,
All happy, happy dreams I bring.
Wake not, but hear me, love!

Of all the world of dreams ’tis thine
This once to choose the most divine.
So choose, and sleep, my love!

But ne’er again in choice be free,
Unless, unless—thou dream’st of me.
